# wireshark-tshark fixture

`firmware-ethernet.hex` and `uart-payload.hex` are handwritten synthetic
inputs. The first has two Ethernet frames with distinct nanosecond UTC
timestamps in reverse chronological order. The second has two UART payloads
without timestamps and is exercised both as opaque and synthetic UDP data.

`networking.pcapng` is generated by `tests/support/build_networking.py` with
Python wire encoders and no packet-analysis library. Its fictional tagged frames
include ARP, IPv6 neighbor discovery, DNS, DHCPv4 and DHCPv6, IGMP and MLD,
multicast UDP, a minimal TLS ClientHello and opaque or incomplete TLS records.
One DNS frame is deliberately truncated, and a request and response use
different VLANs. A lone IPv4 fragment has no captured completion. Frame 1
carries a packet-drop report. An outer UDP/VXLAN frame carries inner TCP, and
two split ClientHello records compare reassembly across mixed and matching VLANs.
DNS over TCP includes a response whose request reassembles across VLANs.
A DHCP offer is reassembled from IPv4 fragments on different interfaces.
`networking-cooked.pcap` holds VLAN 42 on a Linux cooked v2 link header.

`sample.pcapng` is a fictional capture written by `build.py` (deterministic; run
`python build.py` in this folder to recreate it). Eight Ethernet frames between a
host (192.168.7.1) and a board (192.168.7.10):

| Frames | Content |
|---|---|
| 1-2 | ARP request and reply |
| 3-4 | CoAP GET `/sensors/temp`, MID 4660, answered 2.05 Content `23.5` |
| 5-6 | Modbus/TCP transaction 1, Read Holding Registers 0-1, values 235 and 258 |
| 7-8 | CoAP GET `/sensors/humidity`, MID 4661, answered 2.05 Content `41` |

IPv4, UDP and TCP checksums are valid; TShark 4.6.8 reports no expert warnings.
`tests/plugins/wireshark-tshark.test.ts` asks a replay session about it.

`traffic.pcapng` is generated by the same script. It contains two Ethernet observation
interfaces, a TCP handshake followed by retransmission, a gap acknowledged by the peer,
a snaplen-truncated segment, a TCP partial pseudo-header checksum and a bad UDP checksum.
It also contains DNS and HTTP request/reply pairs, an unanswered DNS request and bidirectional
IPv6 UDP. The payload marker is synthetic data used to verify model projection.

`untimed.pcapng` starts with a Simple Packet Block without a timestamp and has two
sections that use the first interface, followed by ordinary timestamped frames.

`automotive.pcapng` is generated by `tests/support/build_automotive.py`. Its synthetic wire
bytes exercise split DoIP/TCP, multiple PDUs in one frame, diagnostic ACK/NACK, an unfinished
TCP PDU, SOME/IP-TP completion and a lone fragment, SD entries with nonzero and zero TTL,
stacked VLANs, two interfaces, saved drops, truncation and an untimed raw-IP frame.
`automotive-coverage.pcapng` contains a completed TCP PDU followed by a pending suffix
and a noninitial IP fragment with an unobserved transport port.
`automotive-mixed-vlan.pcapng` splits a DoIP/TCP PDU and a SOME/IP-TP message across VLANs 42 and 43.
Upstream protocol samples can be supplied independently through
`VERA_WIRESHARK_AUTOMOTIVE_SAMPLES`. Use a directory containing `someip_sd_sample.pcap`,
`someip-udp-method-call.pcapng` and `someip-tp.pcap`. The Wireshark dissector contribution
publishes these samples without confirming their hardware provenance.
[Wireshark #16014](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/work_items/16014)

`comparison-*.pcapng` are generated by `tests/support/make-capture-comparison-fixtures.py`.
The baseline and changed traces bracket a 500 ms window with ARP frames.
The changed trace adds one TCP retransmission, changes an independent UDP tuple,
and increases the upper DNS delay and both HTTP response delays. The equivalent trace has
independently encoded timestamps, sequence numbers and DNS IDs. The unmatched
trace adds a noninitial UDP fragment with no observed transport ports.
The cross-interface and cross-VLAN traces duplicate a TCP segment under different
observation contexts while preserving the original frames. The interface-drop
trace preserves the baseline frames and records interface and operating system
drops in the interface statistics block.
